contributions.detail: The 9 written Schedule A rows on p2 sum to 500.00 + 50.00 + 100.00 + 500.00 + 100.00 + 15100.00 + 25000.00 + 317.96 + 10000.00 = 51,667.96 exactly — equal to the page subtotal, to the sum-of-all-pages total, and to the promoted PER-PERIOD cell Box B. Box C (Year to Date) prints the identical 51,667.96 and is NOT summed as an increment; this is the filer's first report of the cycle so period == year-to-date, which is why the two agree (the §C2 pattern, not an anomaly). The closure also SETTLES row 4 (Greg Smith): its raised cents render at 2000 dpi as an oval plus a hooked glyph that can be read '06', and its third dollar digit has the same hook, so '506.06' is a legible alternative — but 506.06 would give 51,674.02 against a figure printed five times on this document, whereas 500.00 closes to the cent. Arithmetic closure outranks glyph reading (GOTCHAS / Rhodes reversal): the row publishes 500.00 and the ambiguity is recorded in its note. NOTE for the reader: Box A 'Balance at Beginning of Reporting Period' also prints 51,667.96 and Box F 'Subtotal before Expenditures (Box A + Box B)' prints 51,667.96 rather than A+B = 103,335.92 — the filer's own summary-ladder inconsistency, retained verbatim and NOT adjudicated; it touches no itemized row and the contribution side is gated on Box B, which the schedule's own two footers independently corroborate.

THE APPARENT 823.59-vs-43,061.32 CONFLICT FLAGGED TO THIS AGENT IS NOT A CONFLICT: 823.59 is p4's own PAGE subtotal (a page-scoped figure) and 43,061.32 is the sum-of-all-Schedule-B-pages figure — two printed lines of different scope on the same sheet, both correct and mutually consistent, and p3's own subtotal supplies the missing 42,237.73. escalation_note: Ten legibility escalations, all crops named with this filing's key. (1-5) THE DATE-YEAR QUESTION. A corpus-wide OCR sweep flagged apparent '2024' dates on this filing. Read at the page: the filer writes his year-6 as a COMPRESSED HOOK (a down-left diagonal, a short horizontal, then a descending tail that curls) which at 200 dpi is indistinguishable from a 4, while his genuine 4 is a TWO-STROKE PRINTED 4 whose vertical stem rises ABOVE the crossbar. The two forms appear side by side in one cell on p2 row 5, cropped at 2000 dpi (d4741fec_p2r5_date.png): '6/4/26' renders a tall bowl-6, then an unmistakable two-stroke 4 in the day slot, then '2' + the compressed hook. p3 row 7 at 2000 dpi (d4741fec_p3r7_date.png) shows the same contrast within one cell: '4/23/26', printed-4 in the month slot, hook-6 in the year slot. The single date the sweep is most likely to have flagged, p3 row 9, was cropped alone at 2000 dpi (d4741fec_p3r9_date.png) and beside its neighbour (d4741fec_p3r9r10_yr.png): its year glyph has NO stem above the crossbar and matches the hook form, not the printed 4. EVERY date on this filing is /26; NONE is /24; the filing is genuinely 2026 and no reclassification was made. (6-7) The p2 date column was read in two 900 dpi blocks (d4741fec_p2_dates_a/b.png) and the p3 date column in three (d4741fec_p3_dates_16.5/38.9/60.7.png). (8) p2 row 2's MONTH digit is over-written — a 5-form and a 3-form superimposed in the same blue ink (d4741fec_p2r2_date.png, 2000 dpi); the day '09' and year '26' are clear but the month is not uniquely assignable, so the date is left BLANK with needs_review=1 rather than guessed (the ADDENDUM B1 discipline). (9) p2 row 4's amount cell at 2000 dpi (d4741fec_p2_r4amt.png) — the filer's ZERO carries a lead-in hook that reproduces as a 6; resolved to 500.00 by the page's arithmetic, not by the glyph. (10) The p2 Schedule A column heading was cropped at 900 dpi (d4741fec_p2_hdr.png) and renders 'City and Zip Code' — see notes, this is NOT the 'Address and Zip Code' column recorded for the 2024 v. 12.23 stock.
